name: Dubrovnik
tagline: The Adriatic's most complete medieval walled city, marble streets and baroque churches still enclosed by nearly two kilometres of fortifications.
highlight: Walking the full circuit of the City Walls at sunrise, the Old Town's terracotta rooftops glowing below and the Adriatic stretching out on the other side.
shortDescription: The Adriatic's most complete medieval walled city, home to nearly two kilometres of intact fortifications, a marble old town and Fort Lovrijenac.
metaDescription: A Dubrovnik travel guide: the City Walls, Stradun, Fort Lovrijenac, the Srđ cable car, food and how to plan a visit to Croatia's walled city.
knownFor: The City Walls, Stradun, Fort Lovrijenac
budget: €120–250 per day, mid-range (higher in peak summer)

image.alt: Dubrovnik's medieval city walls above the Adriatic

intro: Dubrovnik is the Adriatic's most complete medieval walled city, its Old Town still fully enclosed by nearly two kilometres of intact 16th-century fortifications.

Inside those walls, marble-paved Stradun runs the length of a townscape of baroque churches, monasteries and palaces, almost entirely rebuilt after a devastating 1667 earthquake in remarkably unified style.
It's a city that rewards patience with its crowds — arriving early, staying late, or timing a visit outside cruise-ship hours all transform the experience.

whyVisit.intro: Dubrovnik's case rests on being one of the best-preserved fortified cities anywhere in the world.

points.title: The City Walls are a singular experience
points.text: Nearly two kilometres of intact fortifications, walkable in their entirety.

points.title: The Old Town is remarkably unified
points.text: Rebuilt after a 1667 earthquake in consistent baroque style, marble streets and all.

points.title: The setting is dramatic
points.text: A walled city rising straight from the Adriatic, backed by Mount Srđ.

points.title: It's an easy gateway to the islands
points.text: Ferries connect Lokrum, the Elaphiti Islands and further afield straight from the Old Town harbour.

points.title: It works well outside peak crowds
points.text: Early mornings, evenings and shoulder-season visits reveal a much quieter, more atmospheric city.

attractionsIntro: Dubrovnik's essential sights are concentrated within and immediately around its walled Old Town.

attractions.name: The City Walls
attractions.text: The city's defining feature, nearly two kilometres of intact medieval and Renaissance fortifications encircling the entire Old Town.
attractions.tip: Walk the full circuit early morning, both for the light and to beat the worst of the crowds and heat.

attractions.name: Stradun

image.file: File:Main Street Placa Stradun Old Town Dubrovnik (4058859258).jpg

attractions.text: The Old Town's spine, a marble-paved promenade running the full length of the walled city.
attractions.tip: Visit in the early evening for the classic Dubrovnik ritual of a slow walk and gelato.

attractions.name: Fort Lovrijenac
attractions.text: A dramatic standalone fortress on a cliff just outside the walls, built to guard the city's western approach.
attractions.tip: Climb up for one of the best views back over the Old Town's rooftops and walls.

attractions.name: The Rector's Palace
attractions.text: The former seat of the Republic of Ragusa's government, a Gothic-Renaissance palace now housing the city museum.
attractions.tip: A cool, quiet escape from the heat and crowds of Stradun outside.

attractions.name: The Franciscan Monastery

image.file: File:CLOISTER OF THE FRANCISCAN MONASTERY IN DUBROVNIK, CROATIA.jpg
image.alt: The cloister of the Franciscan Monastery in Dubrovnik

attractions.text: Home to one of the oldest continuously operating pharmacies in Europe, alongside a beautiful Romanesque cloister.
attractions.tip: Don't miss the small museum's collection of historic pharmaceutical equipment.

attractions.name: The Srđ Cable Car

image.file: File:Cable car to Mount Srd in Dubrovnik, Croatia (48738636363).jpg
image.alt: The cable car climbing Mount Srđ above Dubrovnik

attractions.text: The easiest way up Mount Srđ, whisking visitors from the Old Town's edge to a panoramic viewpoint in minutes.
attractions.tip: Go for sunset — the view over the walled city and islands is spectacular.

attractions.name: Lokrum Island
attractions.text: A wooded island retreat a short boat ride from the Old Town, with a botanical garden and rocky swimming spots.
attractions.tip: A lovely half-day escape from the Old Town's heat and crowds.

thingsToDoIntro: Dubrovnik rewards both essential sightseeing and simply slowing down between the walls and the sea.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the full circuit of the City Walls
thingsToDo.text: An essential Dubrovnik experience, circling the entire Old Town with views over rooftops and sea alike.
thingsToDo.tip: Allow at least 1.5 to 2 hours at an unhurried pace, with stops for photos.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the cable car up Srđ Hill

image.file: File:Dubrovnik - kolejka na górę Srd - cable car to Srd hill - panoramio.jpg
image.alt: The cable car up Srđ Hill above Dubrovnik

thingsToDo.text: A quick, rewarding trip, trading the Old Town's narrow streets for a sweeping panoramic view.
thingsToDo.tip: Book tickets online ahead in peak season to skip the queue.

thingsToDo.title: Take a boat to Lokrum Island

image.alt: Boats departing for Lokrum Island from Dubrovnik

thingsToDo.text: An easy half-day escape, a short ferry ride to a quiet, wooded island with a botanical garden.
thingsToDo.tip: Bring water shoes — Lokrum's swimming spots are mostly rocky rather than sandy.

thingsToDo.title: Kayak along the Old Town's sea walls

image.file: File:Kayaks in the Adriatic Sea of Dubrovnik, Croatia (48612968121).jpg

thingsToDo.text: A unique perspective, paddling right beneath the fortifications from the water side.
thingsToDo.tip: Book a guided sunset tour for the best light over the walls.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Stradun at golden hour

image.file: File:Detail Placa Stradun Old Town Dubrovnik 2 (4058270235).jpg
image.alt: Stradun at golden hour in Dubrovnik

thingsToDo.text: A lovely ritual, the marble street glowing warm as the day's heat and crowds finally ease off.
thingsToDo.tip: A nice time for people-watching from a Stradun café terrace.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Franciscan Monastery's cloister

image.file: File:Frecscoes in the cloister of the Franciscan monastery, Dubrovnik (5) (29466173154).jpg
image.alt: The cloister of the Franciscan Monastery in Dubrovnik

thingsToDo.text: A peaceful stop, a Romanesque cloister and historic pharmacy tucked just off the busy Stradun.
thingsToDo.tip: A good midday escape from the heat and crowds outside.

foodIntro: Dubrovnik's food centres on fresh Adriatic seafood and classic Dalmatian cooking.

foods.name: Fresh grilled seafood

image.alt: Grilled seafood at a traditional Croatian restaurant

foods.text: A highlight of dining here, fish and shellfish grilled simply at restaurants throughout the Old Town.
foods.whereToTry: Konobas and seafood restaurants throughout the Old Town.

foods.name: Crni rižot (black risotto)

image.alt: Black risotto made with cuttlefish ink

foods.text: A Dalmatian classic, worth trying at least once during a Dubrovnik visit.
foods.whereToTry: Seafood restaurants throughout the Old Town.

foods.name: Dalmatinski pršut (dry-cured ham)
foods.text: A reliable starter, often served simply with local cheese and olives.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and konobas throughout the Old Town.

foods.name: Peka (slow-cooked under a bell)
foods.text: Worth ordering ahead, meat or seafood slow-cooked with vegetables under embers for hours.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional konobas, especially outside the busiest tourist streets.

foods.name: Pelješac Peninsula wine
foods.text: Worth seeking out, bold red wines from the peninsula just up the coast from Dubrovnik.
foods.whereToTry: Wine bars throughout the Old Town.

foods.name: Fritule (small fried doughnuts)
foods.text: A nice sweet treat, found at bakeries and market stalls around the Old Town.

accommodation.intro: Dubrovnik offers everything from budget guesthouses to luxury hotels, with location making a real difference to the experience.

areas.name: Inside the Old Town walls
areas.bestFor: Being immersed in the historic atmosphere, day and night
areas.text: The most atmospheric base, though also the priciest and busiest during the day.

areas.name: Lapad or Babin Kuk
areas.bestFor: A better-value stay with easy beach access
areas.text: A short bus ride from the Old Town, with a more residential, relaxed feel.

gettingThere.intro: Dubrovnik is well connected by direct flights, with ferries linking it to the wider Dalmatian coast.

options.text: Available from many European cities, especially in summer.
options.detail: Dubrovnik Airport sits about 20 minutes from the Old Town.

options.text: The fastest way to connect from the capital.
options.detail: Takes under an hour, versus most of a day by road.

options.mode: Ferry or coastal bus from Split
options.text: A scenic overland or sea option.
options.detail: Buses take around four to five hours; ferries run less frequently but offer spectacular coastal views.

gettingAround.intro: Dubrovnik's car-free Old Town is entirely walkable, with buses covering the wider city.

options.text: The only way to explore the Old Town itself.
options.detail: No cars are permitted inside the walls.

options.text: Useful for reaching Lapad, Babin Kuk or the airport.
options.detail: A frequent, inexpensive network connects the Old Town to the wider city.

options.text: The easiest way up Mount Srđ.
options.detail: Departs from just outside the Old Town's Ploče Gate.

bestTime.headline: May, June and September for warm weather without peak-summer crowds
bestTime.summary: Dubrovnik is at its most crowded and expensive in July and August, with shoulder months offering a far better balance.

seasons.text: Warm enough to swim, with noticeably thinner crowds than peak summer.
Hot and lively, though the Old Town gets packed, especially on cruise-ship days.
Still warm enough for the sea, with crowds and prices both easing off.
Quiet and atmospheric, though many restaurants and attractions reduce their hours.

bestTime.avoid: July and August's peak crowds and prices, if your dates are flexible.

itinerary.title: Three days in Dubrovnik
itinerary.intro: Built around the City Walls, the wider Old Town, and a slower day exploring beyond the walls.

days.title: Stradun and the Old Town
days.summary: An introduction to the walled city.
days.morning: Arrive and settle in near the Old Town.
days.afternoon: Wander Stradun, the Rector's Palace and the Franciscan Monastery.
days.evening: Dinner with a view of the floodlit walls.

days.title: The City Walls and Fort Lovrijenac
days.summary: The full walls circuit and a viewpoint fortress.
days.morning: Walk the full circuit of the City Walls, starting early.
days.afternoon: Fort Lovrijenac and its views over the Old Town.
days.evening: Sunset from the Srđ cable car.

days.title: Lokrum Island
days.summary: A slower day on the water.
days.afternoon: Swim and explore the island's botanical garden.
days.evening: A final Dalmatian dinner in the Old Town.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Dubrovnik visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book City Walls tickets online ahead to skip the entrance queue.
Walk the walls first thing in the morning to beat both heat and crowds.
Check the cruise ship schedule — some days bring far heavier Old Town crowds than others.
Wear comfortable, grippy shoes — the Old Town's marble streets get slippery when wet.
Book accommodation well ahead for a July or August visit.
Escape to Lokrum or Lapad's beaches when the Old Town feels overwhelming.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Dubrovnik?
faq.a: Three to four days allows time for the walls, the wider Old Town and a boat trip to Lokrum without rushing.

faq.q: Is Dubrovnik worth visiting despite the crowds?
faq.a: Yes — visiting the walls early morning and checking the cruise ship schedule both help enormously.

faq.q: Are the City Walls worth the entry fee?
faq.a: Yes — it's widely considered one of Europe's best walking experiences, with views found nowhere else in the city.

faq.q: How do you get from Dubrovnik Airport to the Old Town?
faq.a: By airport shuttle bus or taxi, taking about 20 to 30 minutes.
Yes — rocky beaches line the Old Town's edge, with Lokrum Island and Lapad's beaches both popular alternatives.

faq.q: Can you day-trip to the islands from Dubrovnik?
faq.a: Yes, easily — Lokrum is a short boat ride, and the Elaphiti Islands make a popular full-day trip.
